children: Tomra Systems stock fell sharply after the French government dropped a policy designed to increase levels of recycling, potentially dealing a blow to the company's operations in the country.
Shares slid over 6.6% in early afternoon trade to 98.90 Norwegian kroner, leading the Europe-wide Stoxx 600's fallers Monday.

A joint statement by ministers Mathieu Lefevre and Francoise Gatel said the government would abandon plans to introduce a mandatory deposit scheme across France. The policy would have required consumers to pay a deposit when buying plastic bottles, with the deposit refunded when the customer returned the container for recycling.
Instead, French regions will be allowed to choose their own policies for increasing recycling.

The policy for a mandatory deposit scheme, announced by President Emmanuel Macron earlier this year, promised to be a boon for Tomra Systems. The Norway-based group produces reverse vending machines, in which shoppers can drop off empty cans and bottles in return for refunds and vouchers.

France is under pressure to reduce plastic waste in order to keep pace with European Union targets on waste reduction. Member states must recycle 90% of plastic bottles by 2029 to meet the EU's targets.
Tomra Systems didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
